title: The Blender-256 entry condition in §3.3 conflicts with Theorem 2
body: I read §3.3 as saying that after eight steps from the standard IV, all four words \(W_0,W_2,W_4,W_6\) lie in \(\{x,\neg x\}\) for the same \(x\). Let \(p_0\) be the parity of the number of bits where \(W_0\) and \(W_2\) differ, and let \(p_4\) be the same parity for \(W_4\) and \(W_6\). Each pair differs in either 0 bits or 32 bits, so \(p_0=p_4=0\). Theorem 2 requires \(p_4=p_0\oplus1\) at every step from the standard IV. title: Does the 24-byte minimum for Blender-256 hold beyond the two-step healing family?
body: Proposition 6 rules out standard-IV collisions between equal-length messages shorter than 24 bytes within the two-step silent-carry healing family. The 24-byte example is therefore shortest within that family. The proposition’s title and final sentence call 24 bytes the global minimum, and the contributions section makes the same broader claim.
